findings.where: Screen 4 say line (coolSay), also shown after Check on screen 3 and on screens 6 and 10
findings.what: The line under the drawing says "NR2 stops water running back through P2" before screen 5 asks exactly that, so screen 5 is answered by re-reading rather than reasoning; keep that clause out of coolSay until screen 5 has been answered.

findings.where: Screen 2 say line and the TI bubble on the cooling sheet
findings.what: "TI the temperature instrument" reads the bubble's letters, which the brief marks UNCONFIRMED, and a bubble lettered TI driving TV1 down a signal line teaches a tag pattern he may meet differently on real sheets; show the bubble without reading its letters (call it the temperature sensor that sets TV1) or quote the letters from a source first.

"Water flows only where a path is open all the way through a running pump" is stated as a general rule, while explain rightly limits it to a pumped system and adds that a higher tank or trapped pressure can push too; begin it "In a pumped loop like this," so the key screen does not teach that a stopped pump means no flow.

findings.where: Whole lesson against brief.md lesson 7 and its misconception list
findings.what: The brief promised the ISO 10628-2 valve set (gate, globe, ball, butterfly, relief) with the older forms to recognise, three DO screens on DOE's honest limits (gate and globe drawn alike, an actuator's action not shown by the symbol, a three-way valve drawn in its fail position), and the letters that tell two like systems apart, but none of these appears; add them, perhaps by trading screen 7, which repeats screen 6, or record in the brief where they went.

findings.where: i7.build.log.md (symbols drawn: pump, strainer, heat exchanger, non-return valve, three-way valve with diaphragm actuator, instrument bubble)
findings.what: The brief says every symbol is checked against two makers' public sheets and listed in the build log, but this log lists no symbol or sheet, so the drawn symbols are unchecked conventions.

"Two pumps push fresh water" says both run, but only P1 runs and P2 stands by; say "Two pumps, one running and one standing by," so the screen 3 puzzle tests reading the drawn state rather than catching a slip in the words.

findings.where: Screen 3 task and the running/stopped labels under P1 and P2
findings.what: The task says "the sheet draws P1 running", but the drawn-state rule taught is about valves, and the labels are the app's live state; say that the running and stopped labels show the plant now, so he does not expect a piping diagram to print a pump's run state.
The puzzle asks what screen 6 has just shown him by tapping TV1, so it tests recall; ask about the middle setting or about the water reaching the equipment uncooled instead.
The red pipes already end at V3 and V4 when the puzzle opens, so the answer is read off the picture; show the red only after the first tap or the first Check, so he traces the pipes himself first.
The part to tap (V7, then TV1) is named in the words but not marked on the drawing; a soft ring on it would show at a glance what to move.
"Pick P2." does not say how to pick it; "Tap P2 to pick it." says what to do.

findings.where: Cooling and fuel sheets at 360 px (tag, legend and plate text)
findings.what: The 340-wide drawing renders at about 293 px in the phone column, so 13 px tags and grey labels come out near 11 px and the 12 px plate and TI text near 10 px; they read clearly in the pictures, but they fall short of the 12 px the lesson itself promises.
